scenario: A financial newsletter publishes only investment strategies that returned more than 20% in back-testing, citing them as validated approaches. A retail investor uses the newsletter's average back-tested return to select a strategy.

data.description: Newsletter features only strategies with back-tested return > 20%. Underlying distribution of all back-tested strategies assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = 30 percentage points.

question: Featured strategies averaged 40% back-tested return. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean back-tested return Î¼ across ALL strategies that were tested (including unpublished ones), and (b) the fraction of tested strategies that get published.
naive_answer: The typical strategy returns approximately 40% since that is the newsletter average.
naive_trap: Only the top 34% of strategies are published. The true mean across all tested strategies is about 7.8% â€” 32 percentage points lower than the newsletter suggests. A retail investor choosing a 'random' strategy from the methodology would expect much lower returns.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(20-mu)/30; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+30*norm.pdf(a)/sf-40 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,-10,10)
assert abs(mu-7.78)<0.5
assert abs(norm.sf((20-mu)/30)-0.3419)<0.01
